en:
A fresh apple. 

Restores a small amount of health when eaten.

A small vial of transparent slight red liquid.

Heals a modest amount of health when consumed.
A quivering lump of blob residue. Someone probably buys these.

A sturdy pair of leather shoes.

Light enough to keep you nimble on your feet.

A pair of heavy iron-shod boots.

Their weight is a burden, but lends surprising resilience.
A shard of raw mana crystal, cool to the touch and faintly lit from within.
A splinter of aetherite, prised from corrupted rock. It hums faintly against the palm.

A lump of raw iron ore, streaked with rust-coloured veins.

Useless until a furnace has had it.

A bar of refined iron, still warm from the furnace.

The starting point of every forged weapon and every plate of armour.
A handful of coal. It burns hot enough to melt ore, and dirties everything it touches.
Wet river clay, kneaded into a ball. It takes a shape and keeps it.
A bead of condensed void, cold in a way that has nothing to do with temperature.
Mana crystal ground to a fine, faintly glowing powder.

A roll of fine chisels and gravers.

Consumed a little at a time by the work of cutting slots into a finished item.
A smith's drawing of a blade, annotated in a hand that assumed the reader already knew how.
A smith's drawing of a breastplate, with the hard part - the fitting - left as an exercise.

A thick stew of whatever was to hand, cooked over an open fire.

Restores health and stamina both, which no potion does.

A straight iron blade, plain and heavier than it looks.

Nothing about it is clever. It does not need to be.

A breastplate beaten out of four ingots and fitted by eye.

It will stop what it stops.

A chart of surveyed land, drawn by hand.

Shows the ground whoever made it walked. Two charts can be joined into one, and any chart can be
copied onto empty paper.

An empty sheet of paper, ruled and ready to be drawn on.

Every try at a survey spends one, and so does copying a chart.

A handful of leaves and roots, pulled up at the wayside.

Bitter, and worth something to anyone who brews.
Dark berries picked off a thorny shrub, still cold from the shade.

A cut reed stalk, hollow and stubbornly straight.

Thatch, baskets and arrow shafts all start here.

A bundle of planks, pegs and a folded vice, tied with cord.

Set it down somewhere flat and it becomes a workbench - once somebody puts the work in.

Planks pegged into a frame two metres wide and three high.

Set it on the ground or on a floor, and it stands as a wall.

Boards laid on two beams, two metres square.

Lay it on the ground, or across the top of walls for the storey above.

Six treads on a pair of stringers.

Climbs one storey, three metres, over six paces.
A milled coin of soft gold, worn smooth by hands that were glad of it.
A sack of threshed grain, still smelling of the field it came out of.
Stone-ground flour, fine enough to take the print of a thumb.

A dark round loaf with a hard crust.

Filling rather than healing, which is what most people actually want from a meal.

A lump of quartz shot through with soft yellow metal.

Heavy for its size, and worth nothing at all until a furnace has separated the two.

A finger of refined gold, still dull from the mould.

Every coin in the world started as one of these.

A small vial of cold blue liquid.

Restores a modest amount of mana when consumed.

A rolled strip of clean linen.

Closes a wound a little, and costs little enough to buy by the handful.

A reed stalk bound with pitch-soaked cloth.

Worn in the light slot, it lights itself when it gets dark and burns for about an hour.

A sack of coarse grey salt.

Keeps meat from turning, which is why it is worth carrying a long way.

A thick cut of meat on the bone, marbled with fat.

Spoils faster than anything but fish.

A slab of meat packed hard in salt.

Keeps for a season, which is what a traveller is really buying.

A jug of thin barley beer.

Safer than most water, and a great deal cheaper than wine.

A stoppered bottle of dark red wine.

Worth more the further it is carried from the vines that made it.

A silver-scaled fish, caught this morning.

Worthless by tomorrow.

A hard wheel of cheese off pasture country.

Heavy and slow to spoil, which is more than can be said for the milk.

A felled trunk cut to length, bark still on.

The heaviest thing anybody carries by choice.

A sawn board, planed on one face.

Every building, cart and workbench starts as a stack of these.

A long beam of seasoned oak, steamed and bent to a curve.

Shaped for one hull and no other, which is why nobody else wants it.

A rough block of limestone straight off the quarry face.

Undressed, and no use to a wall until it is.

A block dressed square, its faces worked smooth.

What walls and towers are actually built of.

A fired clay brick, sanded and slightly uneven.

Cheaper than stone, and worse in a siege.

A fired storage jar with a narrow neck and two small handles.

Unremarkable, and in every house in the world.

A green hide, hair still on and heavy with fat.

Nobody who has carried one in summer carries a second.
A rolled sheet of cured leather, supple and evenly cut.
A shorn fleece, greasy and full of burrs.
A sheaf of retted flax stems, ready for the wheel.
A bolt of plain woven cloth, sold by the length.

A stoppered pot of deep colour, ground from roadside plants.

It stains everything except the cloth it was meant for.

A plain linen tunic worn with a narrow belt.

Warm, and stops nothing at all.

A miner's pick, iron-headed on a straight ash haft.

Nothing comes out of rock without one, and no pick comes back out unblunted.

A felling axe with a wide iron blade.

Turns standing trees into logs, and blunts itself doing it.

A twist of hand-forged iron nails, no two quite alike.

Dull work to make, and it holds everything else together.

An uncut stone still held in the rock it came out of. Which gem it is, only the cut tells - or a
miner with Gem Lore, who can appraise it from the bag.

Worth guessing about until a jeweller says otherwise.

A plain gold band set with a small red stone.

Worked gold that will never be a coin again, and looks the better for it.

A small bottle of bitter herbal draught.

Sets a man on his feet again, which is not quite the same as healing him.

A shard of violet crystal clasped in brass, lit faintly from within.

Spent by work that would otherwise go wrong.

A leather-bound volume with brass corners and a clasp.

Somebody's collected notes, bound well enough to outlive them.

A short blade with a wrapped handle, more tool than weapon.

Someone kept it sharp for years before it was handed on.

Barrel staves strapped over a quilted shirt with two belts and a fistful of nails.

It creaks with every breath, and it will turn a blow that was never going to land well anyway.

Soft leather boots, worn pale at the toes.

They have walked further than you have.

A cage of bent willow with a mana-dusted trigger plate.

Reliable against young Bestia, and hopeless against anything grown.

A thimble-sized vial of pale red liquid, the cork stamped with a beginner's mark.

Heals a little health. Only a novice may drink it.

A thimble-sized vial of pale blue liquid, the cork stamped with a beginner's mark.

Restores a little mana. Only a novice may drink it.

An iron cap riveted to a mail hood that hangs down to the shoulders.

It hides the hair, which is the least of what it is for.

A heavy signet of gold and aetherite, its face still blank, waiting for a name.

Pressed into the wax of a charter, it founds a guild with its bearer as its master. The seal is spent.

A tall oak pole and a banner in the guild's colours, its hem weighted with iron.

Planted in the ground, it is where Rally to the Banner calls the guild. Enemies can cut it down.

A pale feather that never quite settles in the hand.

Crushed, it whisks its bearer to a random spot nearby. Companions are left behind.

A butterfly's wing, dusted in amber scales that glow like embers.

Crushed, it carries its bearer home to where they last set out from. Companions are left behind.
A long flight feather, light enough to lift on a breath.
A curved fang with an edge still keen enough to draw blood.
A ridged horn, broken off clean at the root.
A tuft of soft fur, warm and thick.
A plate of insect shell, hard as horn and light as bark.
A skein of raw silk, finer than hair and stronger than it looks.
A slab of wax comb, still dripping with honey.
A small, swollen gland full of venom. Handle it with care.
A pinch of fine spores that makes the nose itch.
A tough, overlapping scale, cool and smooth to the touch.
A scale as wide as a palm. No blade has ever scratched it, and no fire has ever warmed it.
A round pearl with a soft, sea-green sheen.
A small, heavy stone that glows like a star seen through mist.
A crystal of blue ice that does not melt, not even in the hand.
A smouldering core, too hot to hold for long.
A cold, pale jelly that a spirit left behind.
A splinter of old bone, dry and brittle.
A strip of yellowed linen. Whatever it once wrapped is long gone.
A black shard that seems to drink the light around it.
A curved shell plate that shines like beaten gold, and weighs nearly as much.

A reed shaft with a fire-hardened point and three goose feathers.

Put it in the quiver and any bow will shoot it.

A short bow of bent ash, strung with waxed gut.

Needs both hands and arrows in the quiver.

A boiled leather cap, laced under the chin.

It has stopped one falling branch already, and it has the dent to prove it.

A round of pine planks with an iron boss and a leather grip.

Heavier than it looks, and lighter than what it stops.

A fist-sized stone that fits the hand.

Good for knocking, better for knapping.

A nodule of flint, glassy where it has broken.

Struck right, it leaves an edge sharper than steel.

A dry branch fallen from a tree.

A handle, a kindling, a walking aid.

A flake of flint lashed into a split stick.

It cuts until it does not, and then you make another.

A knapped stone wedged into a stick.

It chops slowly and bruises more than it cuts, but it chops.

A canvas sack under the postal seal. Nobody may open it, the courier included.

Bring it to the post office it is addressed to before its deadline.

A small glass bottle with a cork stopper.

Empty, and waiting to be filled with something better.

Plain water, blessed by a Priest and stoppered in a small bottle.

It burns the undead and anoints a weapon with the holy element.

A small vial of murky green liquid that smells of bitter almonds.

Worked into a blade with Enchant Poison, every cut may leave it behind.

A violet crystal out of a shallow geode. The commonest gem in the world. It is still caught in rock.

Gem Cutting turns it into a cut amethyst.

A green crystal out of deep granite. It is still caught in rock.

Gem Cutting turns it into a cut emerald.

A deep red crystal out of marble. It is still caught in rock.

Gem Cutting turns it into a cut ruby.

A gem that grew in the gas pockets of a cooled lava flow. It is warm to the touch. It is still caught in rock.

Gem Cutting turns it into a cut pyrelith.

The hardest stone there is, from the roots of the oldest land. It is still caught in rock.

Gem Cutting turns it into a cut diamond.

A faceted amethyst. It has no power of its own.

Runic Etching binds an essence of a Bestia up to level 20 into it.

A faceted emerald. It has no power of its own.

Runic Etching binds an essence of a Bestia up to level 40 into it.

A faceted ruby. It has no power of its own.

Runic Etching binds an essence of a Bestia up to level 60 into it.

A faceted pyrelith. It has no power of its own.

Runic Etching binds an essence of a Bestia up to level 80 into it.

A faceted diamond. It has no power of its own.

Runic Etching binds the essence of a Bestia of any level into it.

A cut gem with the essence of a Bestia bound inside. It glows with the creature's power.

It fits into any socket.

A sticky lump of tree resin.

It catches fire easily and burns hot.

A sack of fitted stones and a clay flue, packed in straw.

Set it down and it becomes a furnace - once somebody puts the work in.

An anvil horn, a bellows and a ring of hearth stones, roped together.

Set it down and it becomes a forge - once somebody puts the work in.

Planks, two iron bands and a hasp, waiting to be a chest.

Set it down and it becomes a chest only you can open. Whoever breaks it can take what spills.

Beams for a head frame, a windlass and a coil of rope.

Set it down and it becomes a mining shaft. Your bestias dig the ore below it while you are away.

Kindling, a few stones and a lump of resin to get it going.

Set it down to light a campfire. It burns half an hour, longer with more wood.

A plain short sword with a leather-wrapped grip.

Every new master gets one, and most keep it longer than they admit.

A short rod of polished willow with a copper cap.

It hits poorly, but mana runs down it like water down a gutter.
A knotted oak club. Nothing fancy, nothing to break.
A long-hafted hammer with an iron head. It needs both hands and a strong back.
A bearded axe made for battle rather than for firewood.
A broad two-handed axe. It swings slowly and ends arguments.
A blade as long as a man's leg, held in both hands.
An ash shaft with a leaf-shaped iron head.
An axe blade, a spike and a hook on one long pole.
A tall oak staff, worn smooth where the hands go.
A primer of the first spells, its margins full of someone else's notes.
Stitched leather with iron studs over the knuckles.
A braided leather whip, quick and cruel.
A round-bellied lute with gut strings. It needs both hands to play.
A light crossbow with a goat's-foot lever. Shoots bolts from the quiver.
A short, heavy crossbow bolt with an iron head.
A strap and a pouch. Every master can use one, and every child can.
A smooth river stone the size of an egg.
A light spear made to be thrown. Each throw spends one.
A tall iron-rimmed shield, pointed at the bottom.
A door of riveted plate. Only a knight carries one for long.
Boiled leather over a padded shirt. It creaks.
Riveted rings over a gambeson. Heavy, but it moves with you.

Mana pressed into a heavy, glowing paste.

Laid into the ground in a ring, it holds a ritual.
A smooth, carved stone. Set in the middle of a Mana Circle, it gathers what the ring holds.

Five measures of Mana Concentrate and a focus stone, ready to be laid out.

Placed on the ground it becomes a Mana Circle: up to five helpers join its leader, and after half a minute
of channeling the leader's next skill is charged. The ring is used up by the ritual.

A brass sighting scope and a folding tripod.

Set up on open ground, it is where Cartography surveys the land around it.
A small bottle of black ink. Every try at a survey spends one.
A healing herb of the forest floor. A base ingredient for many potions.
A mana-touched herb that only grows where the mana runs strong.
A tough little herb of the tundra, the taiga and the high mountains.
A sun-dried herb of the desert and the badlands.
A pale herb that only grows on blighted ground.

Beams, a counter, sorting shelves and a post horn, lashed onto a sledge.

Set it down inside a town without a post office, and the post will run it once it is built.

A hall's worth of beams, a long counter and a ledger chained to it.

Trade Post Owner raises it as an auction house, in a town with a post office.

A bent willow switch with a line of twisted bark.

Good for perch and the odd boot.
A light, springy rod of jointed cane.
A tapered ash rod with iron guides. It bends a long way before it breaks.
A thin steel rod with a geared reel. Made for things that pull back.
A striped little fish with a spiny back. Every pond seems to have one more.
A flat, bronze fish that feeds along the bottom. Bony, but filling.
A long green hunter with a mouth full of teeth. Mind your fingers when you take the hook out.
A slick, snake-like fish that keeps wriggling long after it should have stopped.
A strong silver fish with pink flesh. Cooks pay well for a fresh one.
An old, armoured fish from the deep channels. Some say they live a hundred years.
A fast fish with a long, flat bill. It fights the line like a duelist.
Its pale scales glow faintly at night. Alchemists grind them for their brews.
A dark fish that is mostly mouth. It rarely leaves the cold water at the bottom.
A fish with a little light hanging over its head. Nobody knows how deep it lives.
Soaked, rotten and missing its partner. Every angler catches one sooner or later.
A grey piece of wood, washed smooth by the water. It burns well once it dries.
Somebody else's net, knotted beyond use. The cord can still be picked apart.
A bottle with a wax seal and a rolled paper inside. Collectors pay well for one unopened.

A wooden spade on a long handle, its blade hardened in the fire.

Whatever somebody buried, this is how it comes back up.

A hand-drawn map with a circle inked on it.

Something is buried somewhere inside the circle. Whoever digs it up first keeps it.

A treasure map gone brittle and blank.

Somebody has already dug up what it showed.

A blade from before the oldest town still standing, its edge still keen.

The chronicle knows who forged it and whose hands it passed through.

A circlet of worked metal, dented where it was taken from a fallen head.

Kings wore it. The chronicle remembers which.

A heavy signet ring, its seal worn smooth by generations of thumbs.

The chronicle remembers whose hand it sealed for.

A small sealed casket on a chain, holding what someone thought holy.

Nobody has opened it. The chronicle says why it was made.

A thick book bound in boards, its pages brown but still legible.

What is written in it, the chronicle only hints at.

A faded war banner, its device still clear, worn across the shoulders.

Armies marched under it. The chronicle names the battles.

Fence posts, planks and a folded nesting hut, tied with cord.

Set it down and it becomes a Breeding Farm, where a pair of bestias lays an egg.

Reeds, fur and feathers bound into a nest.

A Breeding Farm uses up one for each clutch.

A bestia egg from a Breeding Farm, still warm.

It only hatches in an Incubator.

Fired bricks around an ember core, with a padded nest on top.

Set it down and it becomes an Incubator, which keeps one egg warm until it hatches.
A rare yellow crystal of mana. Dispel burns one to unravel what clings to a target.
A common blue crystal of mana. Endow burns one to carry an element into a weapon.
A small stone carved with a rune of passage. Teleport burns one.
A heavy stone carved with a rune that holds a door open. Warp Portal burns one.
A sheet of fine vellum, primed to hold a spell. Spell Inscription writes an attack onto it.

A scroll with an attack written on it.

Read from the bag, it casts its attack once, with no mana. Spell Training teaches it to a bestia instead.
A red crystal of mana. Stone Curse burns one to turn flesh to stone.

A yew bow with horn tips, made to bring down game.

Needs both hands and arrows in the quiver.
A paper cartridge packed with blasting powder. Blasting sets one on the ground to break the rock.
A plain kitchen-and-camp knife with a wooden grip. Every smith's first blade.
A double-edged dagger with a simple crossguard.
A heavy single-edged knife with a clipped point, made for a fight rather than for bread.
A knife grown nearly to a short sword, still worn at the belt.
A needle of bronze with no edge at all, only a point.
A surgeon's lancet with a hollow groove that carries whatever was last poured into it.
Blackened so it does not catch the light, and balanced for the hand that never misses twice.
A dirk whose hilt hides a small spring that snaps the blade forward on the thrust.
A wavy blade of dark volcanic glass bound to steel. It is colder than the air around it.
Nobody remembers the smith who made it. Nobody it was used on remembers it either.
Strips of linen wound tight around the knuckles.
Leather thongs with a strip of hard hide over the fist.
A bar of iron with four holes for four fingers.
A knuckleduster with a short spike over every knuckle.
Three curved blades rising from a leather gauntlet.
A punching blade with an H-shaped grip, driven straight from the shoulder.
A heavy brass fist, riveted over a padded glove.
Plain iron rings worn on the forearms, worn smooth by a thousand blocks.
A gauntlet set with knuckles of polished granite.
Two gauntlets of grey stone that feel like part of the hand once they are on.
A length of knotted rope with a frayed end that cracks surprisingly loud.
Four strands of leather plaited into a supple lash.
A dried bramble vine bound to a wooden handle. The thorns did not come off.
A drover's whip, long enough to reach the far side of the herd.
Short iron links joined end to end with a weighted tip.
Three tails of dyed silk that sing in the air when they move.
A leather lash with small iron barbs woven into its last span.
Scaled steel links that move like a snake and end in a fanged weight.
A dancer's ribbon of crimson silk, edged with fine wire.
The crack of this whip arrives a moment before the thunder does.
A short straight blade, the length of a forearm.
A broad, leaf-shaped stabbing sword with a round pommel.
A plain cruciform sword, the everyday blade of anyone who expects trouble.
A wide, heavy blade for cutting rather than thrusting.
A light curved sabre with a brass guard, carried by caravan masters.
A long steel blade with a grip long enough for a second hand when it is needed.
A single-edged sword with distance marks etched along its spine.
A slender thrusting sword with a swept hilt. It rewards precision and punishes everything else.
A heavy cleaver of a sword, quenched at sunset in the old way.
A gold-chased sabre that has settled more arguments than any contract.
A small axe for kindling and for anything else that needs splitting.
An axe whose blade hangs low below the haft, good for hooking as well as cutting.
A wide, flat axe head on a short haft.
The axe of the forest wardens, light enough to carry all day.
A smith's test piece: if it holds an edge through oak, the steel is good.
A steel axe with a spike on the back, made for war and nothing else.
A half-moon blade that bites deep and pulls free easily.
A light axe with runes cut along the haft by a hand that knew what they meant.
Dark iron, folded and folded again until it rings like a bell.
Its haft was cut from the heart of a living tree, and it has never quite stopped growing.
An iron head of six flanges on a wooden haft.
A heavy club studded with iron nails.
A spiked iron ball on a short shaft.
A miner's mace with a pick on the back for loosening ore and enemies alike.
A swinging censer on a chain. The smoke it trails is holy; the weight is not.
A mace whose hollow head holds a sealed flask of something better left sealed.
Forged to crack ore that a pick will not, and it does not much care what else it cracks.
A silvered mace blessed over a grave that never stayed shut.
Its head glows faintly an hour before sunrise, every morning, wherever it is.
A straight ash pole sharpened at one end.
A wooden spear whose point was hardened in the coals.
An iron spearhead on a shaft as long as a man is tall.
A broad spearhead with lugs behind it, so the boar stays at the far end.
A lance cut down for fighting on foot, still heavy at the point.
Three barbed tines, made for fish and used for everything else.
A spear with two short wings below its head to stop a charge.
A long pike with a sounding rod hidden in its butt.
A broad-bladed spear with side lugs, for game that bites back.
Its iron head always turns a little toward the nearest vein of ore.
A long, plain blade that needs both hands and a lot of room.
A huge sword with a leather-wrapped ricasso to grip above the guard.
A greatsword with a wavy blade that saws as well as cuts.
A greatsword with a forward-sloping guard ending in quatrefoils.
Square-tipped and perfectly balanced for one kind of stroke.
Good steel, a lot of it, in the shape of a sword.
Runes run the length of the fuller and glow when the blade is drawn in anger.
Its core is a rib from something that breathed fire. It is still warm.
A slab of a sword that splits shields as readily as it splits the men behind them.
It cannot be drawn against anyone its bearer has sworn to protect, or so the knights say.
A splitting maul with an axe's edge, for firewood and worse.
A broad axe head on a long two-handed haft.
The felling axe of a woodcutter who got tired of being robbed.
Two edges, so the backswing is not wasted.
A greataxe with a long hooked beard for pulling riders out of saddles.
A quarryman's axe with a hardened wedge behind the blade.
A crescent blade as wide as a man's chest.
Its haft is ironbark, which no blade has ever cut through.
A double axe a forgemaster makes once, to prove they can.
It follows the grain of the stone, and the stone opens.
A big wooden mallet for driving stakes.
A river stone lashed to a stout haft.
An iron sledge for breaking rock.
A sledgehammer with a flat face and a spiked back.
A smith's great hammer, as at home on an anvil as on a skull.
A maul with a bronze head that never sparks in the gas-filled deep.
A hammer on one side and a pick on the other.
When it strikes the ground, the ground remembers.
A warhammer with a prayer engraved on every face.
Its head was the first anvil of a forge that has burned for three hundred years.
A farmer's hedging blade on a long pole.
A long axe blade fixed to its pole at two points.
A pole blade with a hook for pulling a rider down.
A single-edged blade on a pole, swung in wide arcs.
A pronged hammer head with a spike above it, on a long pole.
A heavy cleaver blade lashed to a pole.
A crow's-beak spike backed by a hammer, for plate armor and what is inside it.
An axe, a spike and a hook on one shaft of good steel.
The ceremonial polearm of a city's wardens, and not only ceremonial.
Legend says it was forged to cut a storm in half. The scar in the clouds over the forge has never healed.
A good straight stick. Every journey starts with one.
An oak staff as tall as its owner, for fighting rather than for spells.
A supple willow staff that bends toward the one who holds it.
A quarterstaff with iron caps at both ends.
The staff of a pilgrim who has walked every holy road twice.
A brass tube full of copper coils. It hums when a spell runs through it.
A fighting staff of ironwood, heavy enough to break a sword.
A staff grown, not carved, from the root of an old tree.
A white staff topped with a lantern that never needs oil.
Six embers were lit from the first fire. This staff holds the seventh.
A twig, trimmed and peeled. It works better than it should.
A pale birch wand with the bark left on the grip.
The wand every apprentice is handed on the first day, and keeps longer than they admit.
A wand carved from a long bone. Nobody asks whose.
A rowan wand capped with a clear quartz point.
A copper rod with a ceramic grip that throws sparks when shaken.
A branch of red coral from a reef no ship has found twice.
A shard of black glass, sharp enough to cut the hand that holds it carelessly.
Iron drawn from where the ley lines cross. Compasses spin near it.
Carved from a fallen star. On clear nights it points to the place in the sky it came from.
A thin book of first words and first signs.
A primer whose every page is singed at the edge.
A worn book of hymns, its spine cracked open at the favourite ones.
Pressed leaves and careful notes on what heals and what kills.
Bound in white leather, with a ribbon for every hour of prayer.
Its pages are grey and powdery, and the writing only shows when it is warm.
Drawings of every creature its author survived, and notes on the ones they did not expect to.
A book of maps where the roads are rivers of power instead of stone.
The rites of the lamplighters, who keep the dark from the door.
Every page is blank until its reader needs it, and then it is the right page.
A short, simple bow of one piece of wood.
A yew bow cut to be drawn quickly from the saddle.
A bow as tall as its archer, with the reach to match.
Its tips curve away from the archer, storing more force than its length suggests.
Horn, wood and sinew, glued in layers by a patient bowyer.
A longbow backed with sinew, which keeps its strength in the wet.
A heavy warbow. Few can draw it twice in a row.
Its string hums a different note for every arrow.
Arrows from this bow seem to ride the wind rather than fight it.
A wooden crossbow spanned by hand. Slow, but anyone can use it.
A light crossbow for birds and small game.
A crossbow with an iron stirrup to brace it with the foot while spanning.
A heavy crossbow with a steel prod.
An all-steel arbalest, heavier than the man who carries it would like.
A short crossbow that can be spanned and shot from a moving wagon.
A crossbow with a magazine on top. Pump the lever and it shoots again.
Spanned with a windlass, and it punches through a door.
Brass gears span it in a heartbeat. The noise gives away the shooter.
Its mechanism ticks like a clock, and it always shoots on the stroke.
A cheap tin whistle with six holes. Play it well and nobody cares that it was cheap.
A flute cut from a riverside reed.
A small skin drum played with the fingers.
A small mandolin, sturdy enough to survive the road.
Loud enough to be heard over a battle, which is what they were made for.
A fiddle that has played at more weddings than it can count.
A war drum whose beat keeps a column marching long after its legs want to stop.
A small harp strung with silver wire.
